title: Roots dance when a coefficient moves
lede: The colored dots are the roots of a polynomial. The diamond is its constant term c, which you can drag. Press Loop c once to send c around the circle through its current position.
notice: The roots move continuously, but after c travels once around the origin they can land on each other's old places: the loop permutes them.
For z³ − c a full loop shifts the three roots cyclically. For z⁴ − c, the four. In z⁵ − z − c, a loop of radius above about 0.54 shifts all five roots; a smaller loop permutes nothing.
Every root is recomputed from the current c, and the readout shows the largest value of |p| at the roots. It stays near 1e-15.
hint: Drag the diamond c around the origin. Colors follow the roots.
